title: Mooie er ny sleityn
description: Ten short stories about the great outdoors: a hill race stopped by lightning, counting seals on the north coast, a picnic in a meadow with a grandfather who loves Brussels sprouts, three nights sleeping out in a glen, a giant and a robber in a storyteller's tale at a ceilidh, a history walk past a Neolithic tomb and a burned brick hunting lodge, geysers and a river delta in Iceland, a painter's diary from a hut on the hills, a new school scheme at an outdoor centre, and a walk to an old chapel on a hilltop where a baby is baptized.

lessons.title: Yn roieder as y tendreil
lessons.summary: Lowri Pengelly, a runner from Ramsey, enters a hill race; the organiser Tavish Munro checks the gear that is required, and Lowri explains her strategy of running slowly up the grassy slopes and fast down; the route is marked with triangular flags, and from the top there is a wide view; then lightning comes, Tavish stops the race, and the runners crouch low on the grassy slope away from the top until the storm passes; next week they run the race again and Lowri is happy with her place.
lessons.text:
Ta Lowri Pengelly ny roieder. T'ee cummal ayns Rhumsaa, as t'ee roie dagh moghrey roish yn obbyr, er ny raaidyn as er ny sleityn. Er y Jesarn shoh, ta roie mooar er ny sleityn, as ta Lowri goll ayn son y chied cheayrt.

Ta'n roie goaill toshiaght ec cass y clieau. Ta mysh three feed roieder ayn, deiney as mraane, aegey as shenn. Ta Tavish Munro ec y voayrd. She eshyn ta stiurey yn roie. T'eh jeeaghyn er dagh roieder as er y poagey echey.

“Ta red ny ghaa shirrit,” dooyrt Tavish. “Ta cooat fliaghee shirrit, as kaart, as feddan beg. Cha nel oo goll er y clieau gyn ad.”

Hug Lowri yn poagey eck er y voayrd. Va'n cooat shirrit ayn, as y kaart, as y feddan. “Mie dy liooar,” dooyrt Tavish. “Vel strateysh ayd?”

“Ta,” dooyrt Lowri. “She shoh my strateysh: roie dy moal seose y lhargagh faiyragh, as roie dy tappee sheese. Ta ram roiederyn roie ro tappee seose, as eisht t'ad roie dy moal er y mullagh.”

“Strateysh vie eh shen,” dooyrt Tavish.

Ta'n raad soit magh lesh bratteeyn beggey trooraneagh, buigh as jiarg. Ta brattagh trooraneagh ec dagh cassan, as ta ny roiederyn eiyrtys orroo. Ghow ad toshiaght. Hie Lowri dy moal seose y lhargagh faiyragh, myr va'n strateysh eck. Va'n faiyr fliugh, agh va'n emshir mie.

Lurg lieh oor, va Lowri er y mullagh. Va'n reayrt reamyssagh: v'ee fakin yn ellan ooilley, as y keayn reamyssagh mygeayrt, as Nalbin foddey ersooyl. Agh va bodjallyn doo çheet veih'n sheear.

Eisht haink y chied tendreil. Va sollys gial 'sy speyr, as lurg shen taarnagh. Haink tendreil elley, faggys da'n mullagh. Ren Tavish sheidey er y feddan echey. “Ta'n roie harrish!” dooyrt eh. “Immee sheese veih'n mullagh! Ta'n tendreil gaueagh er y mullagh.”

Hie ny roiederyn sheese gys lhargagh faiyragh, foddey veih'n mullagh. “Crom!” dooyrt Tavish. “Crom sheese er y thalloo, as ny lhie er y thalloo fliugh. Crom er dty chassyn, as freill dty laueyn ort hene.” Ren dagh roieder crommey sheese 'sy faiyr. Va'n fliaghey trome, agh va'n tendreil goll harrish.

Lurg feed minnid, va'n sterrym ersooyl. Hie ny roiederyn ooilley sheese gys cass y clieau, fliugh agh sauçhey.

Er y Jesarn lurg shen, va'n roie ayn reesht. Ghow Lowri yn strateysh cheddin, as v'ee ny nuyoo. Va boggey mooar er Lowri. “Cha nel tendreil ayn jiu,” dooyrt ee rish Tavish.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Lowri Pengelly jannoo dagh moghrey?
T'ee roie roish yn obbyr, er ny raaidyn as er ny sleityn.
Cre ta shirrit son y roie?
Ta cooat fliaghee, kaart as feddan beg shirrit.
Cre'n strateysh t'ec Lowri?
T'ee roie dy moal seose y lhargagh faiyragh, as dy tappee sheese.
Cre'n reayrt va ec Lowri er y mullagh?
Va'n reayrt reamyssagh: honnick ee yn ellan ooilley as y keayn.
Cre'n aght ta'n raad soit magh?
Ta'n raad soit magh lesh bratteeyn beggey trooraneagh.
Cre ren ny roiederyn tra haink y tendreil?
Hie ad sheese gys lhargagh faiyragh, as ren ad crommey sheese 'sy faiyr.

lessons.title: Coontey ny raunyn
lessons.summary: Eilidh Galbraith becomes a volunteer seal counter on the north coast, under the supervision of the warden Jowan Bolitho; he gives her a booklet about seals and binoculars with good lenses, and tells her an observer must stay far from the animals; the booklet says there are no eared seals in Manx waters, only true seals, and that the spots on a seal are not symmetrical, so each one can be known; the count gives an indirect picture of the fish in the sea, and Eilidh's understanding of the seals grows.
lessons.text:
Ta Eilidh Galbraith er jeet dy chummal ayns Rhumsaa. Ta graih eck er beiyn ny marrey, as t'ee laccal obbraghey dy seyr son y heshaght ta freayll ny beiyn shen. Ta'n heshaght coontey ny raunyn er y traie twoaie dagh mee, as ta feme oc er jeeagheyderyn noa.

Er y chied laa, haink Eilidh gys y traie. Va Jowan Bolitho ayn, yn arreyder. Ta ny jeeagheyderyn noa fo oaseirys Jowan son y chied vlein. “Cha nel oaseirys trome ayn,” dooyrt eh. “T'ou jannoo yn obbyr hene. Ta mish ayns shoh dy reaghey dy vel y coontey kiart.”

Hug Jowan lioaran beg jee. Va jallooyn ayns y lioaran, as fys mychione ny raunyn. “Lhaih yn lioaran shoh 'sy thie,” dooyrt eh. “Eisht hig toiggaltys ort er ny raunyn.” Hug eh fodreayrtan beg jee myrgeddin. “Ta sooillag vie ayns y fodreayrtan shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Lesh y sooillag vie shoh, foddee oo fakin y raun foddey ersooyl.”

“Cre'n fa nagh vel shin goll faggys?” dooyrt Eilidh.

“Shoh yn chied reill,” dooyrt Jowan. “Ta'n jeeagheyder mie freayll foddey ersooyl. My ta raun fakin oo, t'eh goll 'sy cheayn, as ta aggle er. Cha nel y jeeagheyder mie cur aggle er y raun.”

Lhaih Eilidh yn lioaran 'syn oie. Va fys ayn mychione ny raunyn cleayshagh. Ta cleayshyn beggey mooie oc, as t'ad cummal 'sy Cheayn Sheealtagh. Cha nel raunyn cleayshagh ayns ushtey Vannin.

Va red elley 'sy lioaran. Ta ponkyn doo er y chrackan ec dagh raun, agh cha nel ny ponkyn shimmeadragh. Er y fa nagh vel ny ponkyn shimmeadragh, foddee yn jeeagheyder dagh raun y enney.

Mee ny lurg shen, va Eilidh er y traie reesht. Lesh y fodreayrtan, honnick ee kiare raunyn as feed er ny creggyn. Ghow ee jallooyn jeu. Ayns y thie, ren ee jeeaghyn er ny ponkyn ayns ny jallooyn. Va raun ayn as ponk mooar er e kione. “She shen y raun honnick mee er y mee shoh chaie,” dooyrt Jowan. “T'eh er jeet erash.”

“Cre'n fa ta shin coontey ny raunyn?” dooyrt Eilidh.

“Ta'n coontey cur dooin fys neuyeeragh,” dooyrt Jowan. “Ta ny raunyn gee eeast. My ta ram raunyn ayn, ta ram eeast 'sy cheayn. Cha nel shin coontey ny eeastyn hene, agh ta fys neuyeeragh ain orroo trooid ny raunyn.”

Lurg three meeghyn, va toiggaltys mie ec Eilidh er ny raunyn. V'ee enney ny raunyn liorish ny ponkyn oc. Va boggey er Jowan. “Cha nel feme ort er oaseirys nish,” dooyrt eh.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Jowan Bolitho?
She eshyn yn arreyder, as ta ny jeeagheyderyn noa fo'n oaseirys echey.
Cre hug Jowan da Eilidh?
Hug eh lioaran mychione ny raunyn jee, as fodreayrtan lesh sooillag vie.
Vel raunyn cleayshagh ayns ushtey Vannin?
Cha nel. Ta raunyn cleayshagh cummal 'sy Cheayn Sheealtagh.
Vel ny ponkyn er y raun shimmeadragh?
Cha nel. Cha nel ny ponkyn shimmeadragh, as myr shen foddee yn jeeagheyder dagh raun y enney.
Cre'n fys neuyeeragh ta'n coontey cur?
Ta'n coontey cur fys neuyeeragh er ny eeastyn 'sy cheayn.
Va toiggaltys ec Eilidh er ny raunyn lurg three meeghyn?
Va. Va toiggaltys mie eck, as v'ee enney ny raunyn liorish ny ponkyn oc.

lessons.title: Bee 'sy lheeannee
lessons.summary: Ten-year-old Heledd Prothero spends a summer day with her grandfather Iolo Beynon on his farm; first he mows the grass at the edge of the meadow for the animals' winter food, then they eat in the meadow: he fries sausages in fat in a pot over a small fire, and Heledd has brought bread with lettuce, lemonade, plums from the tree and her grandmother's plum pudding; Iolo also brings a box of Brussels sprouts, which Heledd dislikes, so he eats the sprouts and she eats the pudding.
lessons.text:
Ta Heledd Prothero jeih bleeaney d'eash. 'Sy tourey, t'ee goll dy akin e shennayr, Iolo Beynon. Ta thie-eirinee echey er cass ny sleityn, as ta lheeannee vooar faggys da'n thie. 'Sy tourey ta'n lheeannee lane dy vlaaghyn buigh as gorrym.

“Jiu, bee shin gee 'sy lheeannee,” dooyrt Iolo. “Agh hoshiaght, ta obbyr aym. Ta orrym buinn yn faiyr ec oirr ny lheeannee.”

Ghow eh yn yiarn mooar as hie eh gys oirr ny lheeannee. Va Heledd jeeaghyn er. Ren eh buinn yn faiyr ard dy moal as dy kiart. “Cre'n fa t'ou buinn yn faiyr?” dooyrt Heledd.

“Son ny baagh,” dooyrt Iolo. “Ta mee buinn yn faiyr nish, as tra t'eh çhirrym, bee ny baagh dy gee eh 'sy geurey.”

Lurg shen, hie ad gys mean ny lheeannee. Va poagey mooar ec Heledd. Ayns y poagey va arran lesh glassyr, as jough limonaid, as messyn veih'n plumbis ec y thie. Va'n glassyr glass as noa, veih garey Iolo. Va'n limonaid feayr as millish, as va blass geyre beg er.

Ren Iolo aile beg, as hug eh saagh er yn aile. Hug eh sahll 'sy saagh, as tra va'n sahll çheh, hug eh pronnagyn ayn. “Freegh ad dy moal,” dooyrt Heledd. “Cha mie lhiam pronnagyn doo.” Ren Iolo ad y freeghey dy moal 'sy sahll, derrey v'ad dhone as mie.

Eisht ghow Iolo kishtey veg magh. “Ta red elley aym,” dooyrt eh. “Callish Rangagh veih'n garey.”

Ren Heledd jeeaghyn er ny callish Rangagh as ren ee eddin. Ta amvlass eck er callish Rangagh. “Ta amvlass aym orroo,” dooyrt ee. “T'ad sharroo.”

“Ta graih aym orroo,” dooyrt Iolo. “Ver mee ad ooilley dou hene, eisht.”

Va kishtey elley 'sy poagey: puiddin. Va'n puiddin jeant ec shenn-voir Heledd, lesh messyn plumbis veih'n billey. Va'n puiddin millish as çheh foast. Va Heledd laccal y puiddin ooilley.

Ren ad gee ayns y lheeannee. Ren Iolo gee ny pronnagyn as ny callish. Ren Heledd gee arran lesh glassyr, pronnag, as peesh vooar jeh'n puiddin. Ren ad iu y limonaid. Va'n ghrian çheh, as va'n faiyr er oirr ny lheeannee çhirrym.

“Ta'n puiddin share na ny callish,” dooyrt Heledd.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Iolo. “Agh ta amvlass ort, as ta graih aym orroo. Myr shen, ta boggey orrin ooilley.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Iolo Beynon?
She shennayr Heledd eh, as ta thie-eirinee echey er cass ny sleityn.
Cre'n fa ren Iolo buinn yn faiyr?
Ren eh buinn yn faiyr son ny baagh 'sy geurey.
Cre va ayns y poagey ec Heledd?
Va arran lesh glassyr, limonaid as messyn plumbis ayn.
Cre ren Iolo y freeghey 'sy sahll?
Ren eh pronnagyn y freeghey 'sy sahll.
Vel amvlass ec Heledd er callish Rangagh?
Ta. Ta amvlass eck orroo, agh ta graih ec Iolo orroo.
Quoi ren y puiddin?
Ren shenn-voir Heledd y puiddin, lesh messyn plumbis veih'n billey.

lessons.title: Three oieghyn 'sy ghlion
lessons.summary: Steren Roskilly and her younger brother Kenver sleep out for three nights in a glen; on the cold first night Kenver curls up in his sleeping bag, and his wool jacket shrinks when he hangs it too near the fire; the next day he falls on a wet rock and hurts his tailbone, and Steren puts a cold poultice on it; on the second night he gets a cough, and in the dark he nearly takes the laxative from the medicine box instead of the cough medicine, but Steren reads the little container; it is not an illness, only the cold, and they go home happy.
lessons.text:
Ta Steren Roskilly as e braar Kenver goll dy chadley three oieghyn 'sy ghlion. Ta Steren feed bleeaney d'eash, as ta Kenver queig bleeaney jeig. Ta poagey cadlee ec dagh fer jeu, as kishtey veg lesh medshinyn, as sooslagh feeackle, as bee son three laa.

Va'n chied oie feer feayr. Ren ad aile beg ec oirr yn awin. Va jaggad ollan ec Kenver, as v'eh fliugh. Hug eh y jaggad faggys da'n aile dy çhirmaghey. Ren eh cadley 'sy phoagey cadlee echey. Ren eh cribbey 'sy phoagey, gollrish moddey beg 'sy geurey. Ren Steren cribbey 'sy phoagey eck myrgeddin.

'Sy voghrey, ghow Kenver y jaggad ollan. Agh va'n jaggad ro veg nish. “Cre ta er jeet er y jaggad shoh?” dooyrt eh.

“Ren yn ollan crapley,” dooyrt Steren. “Va'n jaggad ro faggys da'n aile. Ta ollan fliugh crapley 'sy çhiass.” Cha row Kenver abyl y jaggad y chur er. Ren y jaggad crapley gys lieh e vooadys.

Er y nah laa, hie ad seose 'sy ghlion. Va ny creggyn fliugh. Huitt Kenver er creg, as huitt eh er e gimmijey. “Ta pian aym 'sy gimmijey!” dooyrt eh. Cha row eh abyl soie sheese er son tammylt.

Ren Steren glabbag. Ghow ee eaddagh glen, as hug ee eh ayns ushtey feayr yn awin. Hug ee yn glabbag feayr er gimmijey Kenver. “Freill y glabbag shoh ayn son jeih minnidyn,” dooyrt ee. Lurg yn glabbag, va'n pian ny sloo.

'Syn oie, va cassaght ec Kenver. Va'n cassaght trome, as cha row eh abyl cadley. “Vel asslaynt orrym?” dooyrt eh.

“Cha nel asslaynt ort,” dooyrt Steren. “T'ou feayr, as shen ooilley. Ta medshin cassaght 'sy kishtey.”

Va'n oie dorraghey. Ren Kenver yn kishtey y osley, as ghow eh saagh beg. Agh ren Steren y saagh y lhaih lesh soilshey beg. “Ny iu shen!” dooyrt ee. “She purgaidagh eh shen, cha nee medshin cassaght! My ta purgaidagh ayd 'sy glion, bee oo roie ersooyl fud ny h-oie.”

Ghow Kenver y saagh elley, as ren eh y medshin y iu. Lurg tammylt, va'n cassaght ny sloo, as ren eh cadley.

'Sy voghrey, ren ad nyn veeacklyn y ghlenney lesh y sooslagh feeackle 'syn awin. Va'n sooslagh feeackle feayr ayns ushtey yn awin. Hie ad thie er yn trass laa. Va pian beg foast ec Kenver 'sy gimmijey, as va'n jaggad ro veg, agh cha row asslaynt erbee er. Tra honnick e voir yn jaggad, dooyrt ee: “Ta shoh nish jaggad son paitçhey!”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren Kenver 'sy phoagey cadlee er y chied oie?
Ren eh cribbey 'sy phoagey, er yn oyr dy row yn oie feer feayr.
Cre'n fa ren y jaggad ollan crapley?
Ren eh crapley er yn oyr dy row eh ro faggys da'n aile.
C'raad huitt Kenver?
Huitt eh er creg fliugh, as huitt eh er e gimmijey.
Cre ren Steren son y gimmijey?
Ren ee glabbag feayr lesh eaddagh glen as ushtey feayr.
Va asslaynt er Kenver?
Cha row. Va cassaght echey, agh cha row asslaynt erbee er.
Cre'n fa nagh ren Kenver y purgaidagh y iu?
Ren Steren y saagh y lhaih, as dooyrt ee dy row purgaidagh ayn, cha nee medshin cassaght.

lessons.title: Yn skeealeragh ec y kaylee
lessons.summary: After a day of walking in the hills, Tressa Mackay goes to a ceilidh in the village hall, where the old storyteller Ruaraidh Sinclair tells a dramatic tale: a robber steals the sheep of a giant on the mountain, and the giant puts a curse on him, so every sheep he takes turns to stone; Tressa asks if the curse was unjust, and the storyteller says the robber did the wrong; at a ceilidh nobody is a passive listener, and after the tale Ruaraidh gives a short talk about the old stories of the hills.
lessons.text:
Va Tressa Mackay er ve shooyl 'sy clieau ooilley'n laa. 'Syn astyr, va kaylee ayns thie y valley. Va kiaull ayn, as arraneyn, as tey as arran. Lurg y kiaull, va skeealeragh ayn: Ruaraidh Sinclair, dooinney shenn lesh folt bane.

“T'eh ny skeealeragh mie,” dooyrt ben ec y voayrd rish Tressa. “T'eh insh skeealyn ec dagh kaylee 'sy valley shoh.”

Hass y skeealeragh seose. Va dy chooilley pheiagh tostagh.

“Foddey er dy henney,” dooyrt Ruaraidh, “va gruagagh cummal er y clieau shoh. Va'n gruagagh mooar, ny smoo na thie. Va kirree echey, kirree bane, as va graih echey orroo.

“Va roosteyr ayns y valley. Cha row'n roosteyr laccal obbraghey. Oie dy row, hie'n roosteyr seose er y clieau, as ghow eh keyrrey veih'n gruagagh.”

Ren Ruaraidh e ghoo y yannoo trome as injil. Va'n skeeal dramadagh, as va ny paitçhyn ec y voayrd jeeaghyn er gyn loayrt.

“Ec y voghrey, ren y gruagagh coontey ny kirree echey. Va keyrrey ersooyl. Cha row boggey er y gruagagh. Hug eh gwee er y roosteyr. ‘Dy chooilley cheyrrey t'ou goaill,’ dooyrt y gruagagh, ‘bee ee ny clagh 'sy laue ayd.’

“Cha row y roosteyr credjal 'sy gwee. Hie eh seose reesht 'syn oie, as ghow eh keyrrey elley. Agh tra ghow eh greim er y cheyrrey, ren ee clagh. Ren eh keyrrey elley y ghoaill, as ren ish clagh myrgeddin. V'eh goaill kirree derrey'n moghrey, as va dy chooilley cheyrrey ny clagh. Shen y fa dy vel wheesh dy chlaghyn bane er y clieau jiu.”

Va'n skeeal harrish. Ren ny sleih bwoalley nyn laueyn.

Dooyrt Tressa rish y skeealeragh: “Nagh row yn gwee aggairagh? Ghow eh keyrrey ny ghaa, as nish cha nel eh abyl goaill red erbee.”

“Cha row yn gwee aggairagh,” dooyrt Ruaraidh. “Ren y roosteyr red aggairagh. Ghow eh red nagh row lesh. Cha row y gruagagh aggairagh, agh y roosteyr.”

Lurg shen, ren Ruaraidh taggloo beg mychione ny shenn skeealyn. 'Sy taggloo echey, dooyrt eh dy row ny skeealyn shoh ec sleih ny sleityn son keeadyn dy vleeantyn. “Ec kaylee, cha nel y sleih fuillaghtagh,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel ad soie fuillaghtagh, gyn loayrt. T'ad loayrt, t'ad gra arraneyn, t'ad cur feyshtyn. Shen yn aght ta skeeal bio.”

Hie Tressa thie fo ny rollageyn. Honnick ee ny claghyn bane er y clieau 'sy dorraghys, as v'ee smooinaghtyn er y gruagagh as er y roosteyr.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va ny skeealeragh ec y kaylee?
Va Ruaraidh Sinclair ny skeealeragh, dooinney shenn lesh folt bane.
Va'n skeeal dramadagh?
Va. Va'n skeeal dramadagh, as va ny paitçhyn jeeaghyn er Ruaraidh gyn loayrt.
Cre ghow yn roosteyr veih'n gruagagh?
Ghow eh keyrrey veih'n gruagagh.
Cre'n gwee hug y gruagagh er y roosteyr?
Dy chooilley cheyrrey ghow yn roosteyr, v'ee ny clagh 'sy laue echey.
Row'n gwee aggairagh, rere Ruaraidh?
Cha row. Ren y roosteyr red aggairagh, cha nee y gruagagh.
Cre dooyrt Ruaraidh 'sy taggloo echey?
Dooyrt eh dy row ny skeealyn ec sleih ny sleityn son keeadyn dy vleeantyn.
Vel y sleih fuillaghtagh ec kaylee?
Cha nel. T'ad loayrt as cur feyshtyn; cha nel ad fuillaghtagh.

lessons.title: Shooyl er y clieau lesh Branwen
lessons.summary: The guide Branwen Vaughan leads a history walk on a hill, and twelve-year-old Cadoc asks most of the questions: first a Neolithic tomb, described in an old treatise written by a vicar in 1780; then a stone cross which, the story says, a man of the nobility put up when he came home from a crusade; then the ruin of a brick hunting lodge of the Earls of Derby, whose earldom held the island, burned by Puritan soldiers, who also brought censorship of plays and songs; last, the place where a farmer found a Roman coin with the name of a consul on it.
lessons.text:
Ta Branwen Vaughan ny stiureyder shooyl. Er y Doonee, t'ee goaill sleih er shooyl er y clieau, as t'ee insh daue mychione shennaghys y clieau. Jiu, ta jeih sleih ayn. Ta Cadoc, guilley daa vlein jeig d'eash, ayns toshiaght y vooinjer, as t'eh cur feyshtyn er dagh red.

Ec y chied ynnyd, hass ad ec claghyn mooarey. “Shoh oaie noalittagh,” dooyrt Branwen. “Ren sleih y traa noalittagh troggal yn oaie, mysh queig thousane blein er dy henney. Ren ad ny marroo oanluckey ayn.”

Ghow ee lioar veg ass e poagey. “Shoh traghtys. Ren saggyrt screeu yn traghtys shoh 'sy vlein 1780. 'Sy traghtys, t'eh screeu mychione yn oaie noalittagh shoh. Hooar eh craueyn ayn, as saagh cray.”

“Vel ny craueyn ayn foast?” dooyrt Cadoc.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Branwen. “Ta ny craueyn 'sy thie-tashtee nish.”

Ec y nah ynnyd, va crosh clagh. “Rere yn skeeal,” dooyrt Branwen, “va dooinney ayn jeh'n ooaslid. Hie eh er y chroshaid gys yn Thalloo Casherick. Tra haink eh thie veih'n chroshaid, hug eh y crosh shoh seose son booise.”

“Vel shen firrinagh?” dooyrt Cadoc.

“Cha nel fys ain,” dooyrt Branwen. “She skeeal eh. Agh va ram jeh'n ooaslid goll er croshaid 'sy traa shen.”

Ec y trass ynnyd, va thie brisht. Va boallaghyn jiarg ayn. “Ta'n thie shoh jeant ass breek,” dooyrt Branwen. “Ta thieyn ny h-ellan jeant ass clagh, agh ta shoh jeant ass breek. Va'n breek cha deyr, as cha row agh ooaslid abyl troggal lesh breek.”

“Quoi va cummal ayn?” dooyrt Cadoc.

“She thie shelg v'ayn son eearley Derby as e vooinjer. Son traa liauyr, va'n ellan ayns laueyn ny h-eearlaght shen. Ec y traa shen, va'n eearlaght niartal. Agh 'sy chaggey, haink sidooryn puritaanagh. Ren ny sidooryn puritaanagh y thie y lostey.” Dooyrt Branwen dy row ny puritaanee goaill kinseyraght lhieu myrgeddin. “Cha row cloieyn lhiggit, as va kinseyraght er arraneyn as er lioaryn,” dooyrt ee.

“Cha mie lhiam kinseyraght,” dooyrt Cadoc.

Ec y kiarroo ynnyd, va magher beg. “Ayns shoh, hooar eirinagh peesh argid veih'n Raue,” dooyrt Branwen. “Va ennym consyl er. Va daa chonsyl ayns y Raue dagh blein, as va ennym y chonsyl er yn argid.”

“Cre'n fa va argid veih'n Raue ayns shoh?” dooyrt Cadoc.

“Ta shen ny feysht vie,” dooyrt Branwen. “Cha nel fys ain foast.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre honnick ad ec y chied ynnyd?
Honnick ad oaie noalittagh.
Quoi screeu yn traghtys?
Ren saggyrt screeu yn traghtys 'sy vlein 1780.
Cre'n skeeal t'ayn mychione y crosh clagh?
Hug dooinney jeh'n ooaslid y crosh seose tra haink eh thie veih'n chroshaid.
Cre'n fa ta'n thie shelg jeant ass breek?
Va'n thie son eearley Derby, as va'n eearlaght berçhagh.
Quoi ren y thie y lostey?
Ren sidooryn puritaanagh y thie y lostey.
Cre va er yn argid veih'n Raue?
Va ennym consyl er yn argid.

lessons.title: Yn geeser
lessons.summary: Tegwyn Menhinick goes on his pension after forty years of work, and he and his wife Ebrel use the first pension money for a trip to Iceland; they watch a geyser throw hot water into the air every few minutes, and the guide warns them about the acidity of some hot pools; they see colourful pools, walk through a tubular cave made by hot rock long ago, and go on a boat that is launched from a black beach into a river delta; the guide says the village invested money in commercial boats for visitors, and Ebrel says the pension is well spent.
lessons.text:
Va Tegwyn Menhinick gobbraghey ayns Doolish son daeed blein. 'Sy vlein shoh, hie eh magh er penshyn. Er y chied laa er penshyn, dooyrt e ven Ebrel rish: “Nish ta traa ain. C'raad t'ou laccal goll?”

“Ta mee laccal fakin geeser,” dooyrt Tegwyn. “Geeser firrinagh, ayns Eeslynn.”

Myr shen, ghow ad yn chied argid veih'n penshyn as hie ad gys Eeslynn.

Er y nah laa, hie ad dys boayl as geeser ayn. Va thalloo lheeah mygeayrt y geeser, as va gaal çheh çheet ass. Hass ad as ad jeeaghyn. Lurg queig minnidyn, hug y geeser ushtey çheh seose 'syn aer, ny s'yrjey na thie. Va boggey mooar er Tegwyn. “Ta'n geeser shoh cur magh ushtey dagh queig ny shey minnidyn,” dooyrt y stiureyder, ben aeg.

Va ushtaghyn beggey çheh mygeayrt y geeser. Va ny ushtaghyn daahoil: gorrym, glass as buigh. “Ny cur dty laue 'syn ushtey,” dooyrt y stiureyder. “Ta'n ushtey feer çheh, as ta geyrid ayns paart jeh ny ushtaghyn. Ta'n geyrid lostey yn crackan.”

“Vel y geyrid ayns ny ushtaghyn daahoil?” dooyrt Ebrel.

“Ta,” dooyrt y stiureyder. “Ta ny daahyn çheet veih'n geyrid as veih bea veg 'syn ushtey.”

Er yn trass laa, hie ad stiagh ayns ooig. Va'n ooig feddanagh, gollrish feddan mooar fo'n thalloo. “Va clagh çheh roie trooid y boayl shoh foddey er dy henney,” dooyrt y stiureyder. “Tra va'n clagh feayr, va'n ooig feddanagh shoh fo'n thalloo.” Hie ad shooyl trooid yn ooig feddanagh lesh soilshaghyn beggey.

Er y kiarroo laa, hie ad gys traie doo. Va awin vooar çheet gys y cheayn ayns shen, as deltey reamyssagh ec beeal yn awin. Va baatey er y traie. Ren ny deiney y baatey y lhunn 'sy cheayn. “Ta orrin y baatey y lhunn dy tappee, roish my hig y tidey,” dooyrt fer jeu. Tra va'n baatey 'sy cheayn, hie ad seose 'sy deltey. Honnick ad ushag, as raunyn er ny creggyn.

“Ta ram lhongyn traghtalagh ayns shoh nish,” dooyrt y stiureyder. “Dy henney, va'n valley shoh boght. Eisht ren y valley baihaghey argid ayns lhongyn traghtalagh son keayrtee. Ren ad baihaghey ayns thieyn-oast myrgeddin. Nish ta obbyr ec ny sleih aegey.”

'Sy fastyr, va Tegwyn as Ebrel soie ec yn uinnag 'sy thie-oast. “Va shen yn argid share veih'n penshyn,” dooyrt Ebrel.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va traa ec Tegwyn?
Hie eh magh er penshyn lurg daeed blein dy obbyr.
Cre ren y geeser dagh queig ny shey minnidyn?
Hug y geeser ushtey çheh seose 'syn aer.
Cre'n fa nagh dod ad cur nyn laueyn 'syn ushtey?
Va'n ushtey feer çheh, as va geyrid ayns paart jeh ny ushtaghyn.
Cre'n daah va er ny ushtaghyn beggey?
Va ny ushtaghyn daahoil: gorrym, glass as buigh.
Cre'n cummey va er yn ooig?
Va'n ooig feddanagh, gollrish feddan mooar fo'n thalloo.
C'raad hie yn baatey?
Ren ny deiney y baatey y lhunn, as hie eh seose 'sy deltey.
Cre ren y valley dy chosney argid?
Ren y valley baihaghey argid ayns lhongyn traghtalagh son keayrtee.

lessons.title: Lioar-laa peinteyr er y clieau
lessons.summary: In her diary, the painter Catriona Lindsay writes about four days alone in a small hut on the hills: she paints in oil and chooses a figwort plant by the stream, with veined leaves, as her subject; she paints the fine veins slowly and no longer wants to make a plant prettier with bright colours, like make-up on a face; in the evening she reads a book on aesthetics that her friend Effie, a skilful old painter, gave her, and on a rainy morning she listens to a harp concerto on the radio; on the last day the painting is finished, and she writes that if she were in town she would not have seen the plant at all.
lessons.text:
Jelune. Ta mee ayns y thie beg er y clieau. Ta mee ayns shoh my lomarcan son kiare laa, dy yannoo peint. Cha nel ushtey çheh ayn, as cha nel soilshey lectragh ayn, agh ta'n reayrt aalin. Ta mee er choyrt lhiam peint ooil, as radio beg. Ta mee peint lesh ooil son feed blein. Ta peint ooil trome as bog, as t'eh goaill traa liauyr dy çhirmaghey.

Jemayrt. Hooar mee my chooish jiu: lus beg ec oirr yn strooan. She farym eh. Ta'n farym ard as glass, as ta blaaghyn beggey dhone er. Ta ny duillagyn echey cuishlinagh: ta ny cuishlinyn gollrish raaidyn beggey 'sy duillag. Hoie mee sheese 'sy faiyr, as ren mee toshiaght er peint y farym lesh ooil.

Ta ny cuishlinyn feer veggey, as ta mee peint dy moal. Tra va mee aeg, va mee laccal jannoo lus ny s'aalin na v'eh, lesh daahyn gial, gollrish cosmaid er eddin. Nish cha nel mee laccal cosmaid 'sy peint. Cha nel mee ceau cosmaid er y clieau, as cha nel cosmaid er y farym.

'Syn astyr, lhaih mee lioar mychione aesthetaght. Hug Effie y lioar dou. She peinteyr schleioil v'ayn, as ish shenn nish. Ta aesthetaght bentyn rish aalid: cre ta jannoo red aalin? Ta Effie gra nagh vel aesthetaght ayns lioaryn ynrican. “Jeeagh er y lus,” dooyrt ee keayrt. “Shen y chied lessoon 'syn aesthetaght.” Ta Effie feer schleioil lesh peint ooil, ny s'schleioil na mish.

Jecrean. Va fliaghey ayn 'sy voghrey, as va mee 'sy thie. Ren mee eaishtagh rish consherto er y radio. She consherto son claasagh v'ayn. Va'n claasagh gollrish ushtey 'sy strooan. Tra va'n consherto harrish, va'n fliaghey ersooyl, as hie mee magh reesht gys y farym.

Va ny duillagyn cuishlinagh fliugh, as va'n ghrian orroo. Va ny cuishlinyn soilshey 'sy ghrian. Ren mee peint dy tappee.

Jerdein. Ta'n peint jeant. Cha nel eh feer aalin, agh t'eh firrinagh. Ta'n farym ayn, as ny duillagyn cuishlinagh, as y strooan.

Dy beign ayns Doolish jiu, cha beign fakin y lus shoh. Cha beign soie 'sy faiyr fliugh, as cha beign eaishtagh rish y consherto 'sy thie beg. Ta mee goll thie er y Jeheiney, agh hig mee erash.

Feyshtyn:
Cre lesh ta Catriona peint?
T'ee peint lesh ooil.
Cre'n lus t'ayns y peint eck?
Ta farym ayn, lus beg ec oirr yn strooan.
Vel Catriona laccal cosmaid 'sy peint eck?
Cha nel. T'ee laccal peint y farym myr t'eh, gyn cosmaid.
Quoi hug y lioar mychione aesthetaght jee?
Hug Effie y lioar jee, peinteyr schleioil.
Cre ren Catriona ec y traa va'n fliaghey ayn?
Ren ee eaishtagh rish consherto er y radio.

lessons.title: Yn skeim noa 'sy ghlion
lessons.summary: Derwa Treweek runs an outdoor centre in a glen, and a new government scheme sends a school group there every week; an adviser comes to see the centre, and explains that her role is only consultative: she gives advice, and Derwa decides; the cleaner Iestyn says the long corridor is full of mud from shoes, and the adviser suggests a place for shoes at the door; the centre does its own catering for forty children; on a rainy day the children play doubles in the hall; and at night Derwa's dog wears a collar with a small light.
lessons.text:
Ta Derwa Treweek stiurey thie mooie ayns glion. Ta paitçhyn scoill çheet gys y thie dy gholl er ny sleityn, dy hroggal claghyn as dy chadley mooie. 'Sy vlein shoh, ta skeim noa ec y reiltys. Fo'n skeim, ta dagh scoill 'sy çheer çheet gys y glion son shiaghtin.

Er y chied Jelune fo'n skeim noa, haink coyrleyder veih'n reiltys. She ben aeg v'ayn, lesh lioar veg. “Ta mee ayns shoh dy chur coyrle,” dooyrt yn coyrleyder. “Ta currym coyrlagh aym ynrican. Ta mee cur coyrle, agh she uss ta reih.”

“Ta shen mie,” dooyrt Derwa. “Ta coyrle mie dy kinjagh, as ta mish reih.”

Hie ad trooid y thie. Va'n corradoyr liauyr as lheean, as va laare clagh ayn. Va Iestyn ayns y corradoyr. She eshyn yn glenneyder. “Ta mee glenney yn corradoyr shoh three keayrtyn 'sy laa,” dooyrt y glenneyder. “Ta ny paitçhyn çheet stiagh lesh ny braagyn oc, as ta ooir er y laare ooilley.”

Ren yn coyrleyder smooinaghtyn. “Ta coyrle aym, agh ta'n currym aym coyrlagh,” dooyrt ee. “Cur boayl son ny braagyn ec y dorrys. Ta ny paitçhyn cur jeu ny braagyn oc roish y corradoyr.” Va boggey er y glenneyder.

Lurg shen, hie ad gys y chuishlin. “Vel shiu jannoo yn lhongeydys hene?” dooyrt yn coyrleyder.

“Ta,” dooyrt Derwa. “Ta'n lhongeydys ooilley jeant ayns shoh. Ta daeed paitçhey ayn dagh shiaghtin, as ta bee çheh oc three keayrtyn 'sy laa. Ta'n lhongeydys yn obbyr smoo 'sy thie.”

Er y Jemayrt, va fliaghey trome ayn. Cha row ny paitçhyn abyl goll er ny sleityn. Hie ad gys y thie mooar, as ren ad cloie doobley. Va daa phaitçhey er dagh çheu jeh'n lhieen. “She doobley share na singyl,” dooyrt guilley beg. “T'ou cloie lesh dty charrey.”

'Syn oie, hie Derwa mygeayrt y thie lesh y moddey eck, Rolo. Va coillar jiarg er Rolo, as soilshey beg 'sy coillar. Ren ny paitçhyn fakin y soilshey 'sy dorraghys. “Cre'n fa ta soilshey ayns y coillar?” dooyrt inneen.

“Son dy vel Rolo doo,” dooyrt Derwa. “Gyn y soilshey 'sy coillar, cha nel shiu fakin eh 'syn oie.”

Ec jerrey ny shiaghtin, screeu yn coyrleyder lettyr. “Ta'n skeim gobbraghey dy mie ayns y glion,” screeu ee.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n skeim noa jannoo?
Fo'n skeim, ta dagh scoill 'sy çheer çheet gys y glion son shiaghtin.
Cre'n currym t'ec yn coyrleyder?
Ta currym coyrlagh eck ynrican: t'ee cur coyrle, as ta Derwa reih.
Cre'n fa ta'n glenneyder glenney yn corradoyr three keayrtyn 'sy laa?
Ta ny paitçhyn çheet stiagh lesh ny braagyn oc, as ta ooir er y laare.
Quoi ta jannoo yn lhongeydys?
Ta'n lhongeydys ooilley jeant 'sy thie hene.
Cre ren ny paitçhyn er y Jemayrt?
Ren ad cloie doobley 'sy thie mooar.
Cre'n fa ta soilshey ayns coillar Rolo?
Son dy vel Rolo doo, as gyn y soilshey cha nel ad fakin eh 'syn oie.

lessons.title: Yn raad gys y cheeill er y clieau
lessons.summary: Lowena Gilmour and her friend Padraig walk the old path of the worshippers to a small ruined chapel on a hill, where long ago a holy man lived in isolation; Lowena's bag is too heavy, so Padraig tells her to lighten it; her ankle swells, and he lends her his stick; at the chapel they see something unusual: worshippers have come up the hill for a baby to be baptized with water from the old well; Lowena is happy, and on the way down she says the isolation of the holy man was not so hard, with a view like that.
lessons.text:
Ta keeill veg brisht er mullagh y clieau. Foddey er dy henney, va dooinney casherick cummal ayns shen ayns lhehlys. Cha row eh fakin sleih elley son meeghyn. Rish keeadyn dy vleeantyn, va ooashleyderyn shooyl seose gys y cheeill er yn raad shenn. Jiu, ta Lowena Gilmour as e charrey Padraig shooyl er raad ny ooashleyderyn.

Va poagey trome ec Lowena. Ec y gleashtan, roish my ghow ad toshiaght, dooyrt Padraig: “Eddrymee yn poagey ayd. Cre t'ayn?”

Ren Lowena y poagey y osley. Va three lioaryn ayn, as bee son three laa, as cooat mooar. “Eddrymee eh,” dooyrt Padraig reesht. “Cha nel feme ayd er three lioaryn er y clieau.” Hug Lowena ny lioaryn as y cooat mooar ayns y gleashtan, as ren ad eddrymaghey yn poagey. Va'n poagey eddrym nish.

Lurg oor er y raad, haink pian ayns cass Lowena. Ren ee jeeaghyn er. Va att er e cass. “Ta att ort,” dooyrt Padraig. “Ta dty chass attit.”

“Cha nod mee shooyl gys y mullagh,” dooyrt Lowena.

Va maidjey shooyl ec Padraig. “Yeeassee dou yn maidjey ayd,” dooyrt Lowena. “Yeeassee dou eh, son y mullagh.”

“Ta mee yeeassaghey dhyt eh son y laa,” dooyrt Padraig, “as ver oo erash eh dou ec y gleashtan.” Ghow Lowena y maidjey, as v'ee abyl shooyl reesht dy moal.

Ec y mullagh, va'n keeill veg. Agh va red anoayshagh ayn: va sleih ayn hannah, mysh feed dy ooashleyderyn. Va saggyrt ayn, as ben aeg lesh lhiannoo beg. “Cre ta jannoo ayns shoh?” dooyrt Padraig rish shenn ven.

“Ta'n lhiannoo goll dy ve bashtit,” dooyrt y ven. “Ta çhibbyr shenn ec y cheeill, as ta'n ushtey casherick. Va'n lhiannoo shoh bashtit 'sy cheeill 'sy valley hannah, agh ta'n moir laccal ushtey veih'n çhibbyr shoh myrgeddin. Ta shen anoayshagh, ta fys aym. Cha row lhiannoo erbee bashtit ayns shoh son keead blein.”

Ghow y saggyrt ushtey veih'n çhibbyr, as hug eh er kione y lhiannoo. Ren ny ooashleyderyn padjer, as eisht ren ad gra arrane. Va'n ghrian soilshean, as va'n keayn gorrym fo'n clieau.

Va Lowena maynrey. “Ta mee maynrey dy ren shin shooyl gys shoh jiu,” dooyrt ee.

Er y raad sheese, dooyrt ee rish Padraig: “Va'n dooinney casherick cummal ayns lhehlys son bleeantyn. Agh lesh reayrt myr shen, cha row y lhehlys echey cha creoi.”

“Ta mee maynrey myrgeddin,” dooyrt Padraig. “Agh ver oo erash my vaidjey.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va cummal 'sy cheeill foddey er dy henney?
Va dooinney casherick cummal ayn ayns lhehlys.
Cre dooyrt Padraig mychione y poagey?
Dooyrt eh: “Eddrymee yn poagey ayd.”
Cre haink er cass Lowena?
Haink att er e cass, as va'n chass attit.
Cre hug Padraig da Lowena?
Ren eh yeeassaghey e vaidjey shooyl jee son y laa.
Cre'n red anoayshagh va ec y cheeill?
Va ooashleyderyn ayn, as va lhiannoo goll dy ve bashtit lesh ushtey veih'n çhibbyr.
Va Lowena maynrey?
Va. V'ee maynrey dy row ad er shooyl gys y cheeill.
